cards.title: CONCEPT
cards.text: Two POV TikTok replications for the Vivienne, 3 headline variants each, SIX FINISHED ADS BUILT 2026-08-27. Animated on Google Omni i2v from the approved keyframes, assembled at 1080x1920 / 24fps CFR, original TikTok music muxed. Colorway Chocolate, $149.99, pre-order, ships October. Ad A runs 36.08s, Ad B runs 9.87s. Files in products/vivienne/pov/final/.

cards.text: NOTES

cards.title: BUILT — 6 FINISHED ADS
cards.text: A1 Nobody can tell what this cost. A2 There is no logo anywhere on it. A3 It only gets better beaten up. B1 the no logo girl bag. B2 the $149.99 leather girl bag. B3 the real leather girl bag. All 1080x1920, 24fps CFR, single encode pass, original sound on each.

cards.title: OMNI QA + RE-ROLLS
cards.text: House rule says hero-product beats never go to Omni because it mutates the product, and every beat here is a hero-product beat. Brooks called Omni, so it ran with a per-clip QA pass at each clip's trim point. First pass: 8 of 13 held. Five failed (macro drift, the open flap re-closing itself, contents rearranging) and were re-rolled once with a hard motion budget. All 13 passed the second pass, including the open flap holding its state with a bare post and zero ovals on the band.

cards.title: NO KEN BURNS
cards.text: Failing beats were NOT filled with zooming stills. The 8/22 law's order of resort is real footage, then approved b-roll, then Omni, then cut the beat. There is no filmed unit (pre-order) and the supplier footage cannot ship, so the fix was an Omni re-roll with restrained motion.

cards.title: APPROVAL GATE
cards.text: These 17 keyframes ARE the approval step. Nothing renders until Brooks signs off on this board.

cards.title: v3 — PRODUCT CONSISTENCY FIX
cards.text: Brooks flagged that the bag looked different in every frame. Cause: v2 anchored on the burgundy TikTok photo and passed the approved Chocolate only as a colour hint, so the engine re-invented the bag's character per frame. v3 drops the burgundy seeds entirely and makes the approved Chocolate three-quarter the single product reference in all 17 prompts, with a locked parts list read off that exact image. See CONSISTENCY-CHECK.jpg: reference first, then five frames.

cards.title: OPEN QUESTION — NEEDS BROOKS
cards.text: What is the interior? Colour, material, pockets. No photo we hold shows inside the bag, so every interior beat is rendered as packed contents over deep shadow and asserts nothing. If the factory sample comes back with a cream twill lining, A7, A8 and all of Ad B need a re-roll.

cards.title: LAW-FORCED DEVIATIONS
cards.text: 1) Ad A's title card says 'Mulberry Bayswater Dupe'. Competitor naming is banned outside the roundup carve-out, so all three A headlines carry a verdict instead. 2) Ad A's 'look at all that room' is an uncleared capacity claim, replaced with the cleared wording. 3) Both references use a black bag and Black's strap treatment is unconfirmed, so Chocolate is used throughout. 4) Every variant carries Ships October, the pre-order law. 5) Ad B beat 4 swaps the reference's camera for our brass closure so the product stays on screen.

cards.title: MUSIC
cards.text: Original sounds preserved. Ad A is 'video games'. Ad B is 'original sound' by :. M .:. Both converted to mp3 and sliced per beat, ready to pass into the animation step so the track bakes in and no audio remix is needed.

cards.title: RENDER COST
cards.text: About 1,900 Higgsfield credits at ~24cr/s for Seedance 2.5. Balance is 3,404. The three variants of each ad share one body render and differ only in the opening card, which is what keeps it affordable.

cards.title: SELF AUDIT
cards.text: Six-month test: passes. No season, no calendar beat. Unboxing and what's-in-my-bag are evergreen formats. Swap test: passes. Every headline stands on a Velantra physical fact (no logo anywhere, all vegetable-tanned leather with no canvas, $149.99, aged brass).
